Problem.description: An RFC 9457 problem document. This is the entry point's default error shape, which a host-supplied ErrorResponder may replace.

detail.description: A longer explanation of this occurrence, present only when the answering module has one to give. It may be a sentence rendered in the request language or a language-neutral token such as "forbidden", so clients must not parse it.

instance.description: A URI identifying this occurrence; absent when there is none to give.

status.description: The HTTP status code the response is written with, repeated from the status line.

title.description: A short summary of the kind of problem. A module that sets none gets the standard English status text for the status code.

type.description: The machine-readable code identifying the kind of problem. A module that sets none gets the RFC 9457 default about:blank; codes this platform defines are URNs of the form urn:speed:<capability>:<code>.

SettingsTenantAdminSetting.description: One declared setting item as the tenant management surface shows it. The declaration fields and the item's control metadata come from the key table; the three value fields come from the tenant layer's rows and the global layer's rows, and every value-bearing field is text in the declared type's own form.

control.description: The control the surface renders for the item.

danger.description: How destructive turning the item off is: "critical" when the surface must confirm the change first, empty when there is no such warning.

description.description: The item's description, rendered in the request's language from the declaration's key, falling back to the declared English text when no localizer is assembled.

effect.description: When a change to the item takes effect: "immediate" when it applies as soon as it is saved, "next-sign-in" when it applies to a member at the next sign-in, empty when the declaration names none.

effective_value.description: The text the item resolves to: the platform policy OR the tenant policy, in the declared type's text form. The mask string for a sensitive item.

has_row.description: Whether the tenant layer holds an explicit row for the item, whether or not the platform policy is forcing the effective value.

key.description: The full setting key: the declaring module's namespace joined with the item's own segment by a dot.

locked_by_platform.description: Whether the platform layer holds this policy on, so that a tenant write turning it off answers 409 tenant-admission-enforced.

platform_value.description: The global layer's value in the declared type's text form, the declared default when the global layer holds no row. The mask string for a sensitive item.

source.description: The layer the effective value comes from: "global" when the platform policy is on or the global layer holds a row, "tenant" when the tenant holds a row and the platform is not forcing the item, "default" when neither holds a row.

tenant_access.description: How much of the item the tenant surface exposes: "read" for a visible but unwritable item, "read-write" for one the tenant may change.

tenant_value.description: The tenant layer's value in the declared type's text form, the declared default when the tenant holds no row. The mask string for a sensitive item.

title.description: The item's title, rendered in the request's language from the declaration's key, falling back to the declared English text when no localizer is assembled.

type.description: The declared type's name as reflection reports it. The tenant surface renders switches, so this is "bool".

SettingsTenantAdminSettings.description: The tenant settings surface's read answer: the declared items it exposes and whether the tenant's settings may be written at all.

read_only_reason.description: Why the surface is read-only, empty when writable is true. The closed set is the refusal code this capability writes for the same condition: "protected" when the host's settings write seam refuses the tenant, "unavailable" when the seam cannot answer. The listing still answers 200 with the settings it read in both cases.

settings.description: The items whose declarations expose them to a tenant, each with its platform value, tenant value and effective value.

writable.description: Whether this tenant's settings may be written through this surface. False when the host's settings write seam refuses the tenant, in which case every write route answers 403 protected, and when the seam cannot answer, in which case every write route answers 503.

get.description: Returns the items whose declarations expose them to a tenant: a schema that declares itself tenant-facing and an item that states a tenant access. No namespace is included or excluded by its name. Each item carries the platform layer's value, the tenant layer's value and their boolean OR, its control metadata, whether the platform layer locks it, whether the tenant layer holds a row, and the layer the effective value comes from. Titles and descriptions are rendered in the request's language. The envelope also says whether the host's settings write seam would accept a write to this tenant. A failure to read either layer, or to ask the seam, answers 503 rather than leaving an item out.

parameters.description: The tenant's name in the path. The path-tenant layer resolves it to the internal identifier before the handler runs; the layer and the policy domain are both fixed to that tenant, and a "layer" or "tenant" query parameter is refused with 400.
parameters.name: tenant

200.description: The items the declarations expose to a tenant

400.description: A layer or tenant query parameter was sent, or the tenant in the path is outside the tenant identifier's value domain

403.description: The caller holds no settings.tenant.read in the tenant's domain

get.summary: List the declared settings the tenant surface exposes

delete.description: Drops the layer of the tenant in the path's explicit row for the setting named by the namespace and key path segments. The full key `<namespace>.<key>` must match a declared item the tenant surface exposes. A key with no tenant access, whether undeclared or declared on the platform surface alone, is 404 — the same answer an undeclared key gets. An item declared read-only is 403 read-only: it is visible, and the refusal names why the row cannot be dropped rather than hiding the item. Deleting a row the layer does not hold is not an error. Dropping the tenant row while the platform layer holds the policy on is allowed: the effective value stays on, so there is no disable to refuse. The host's settings write seam is asked before anything is changed; a refusal is 403 protected and an unreadable answer is 503. A mandatory audit row is written before the change, and if it cannot be written the row is left in place and the answer is 503. The change is attributed to the caller's accountability key, which under an impersonation is the administrator making the request rather than the account impersonated. Success is 204 with no body.

parameters.description: The tenant's name in the path. The path-tenant layer resolves it to the internal identifier before the handler runs; the row is dropped from that tenant's settings layer, and a "layer" or "tenant" query parameter is refused with 400.
parameters.name: tenant

parameters.description: The namespace of the item whose row is dropped: the declaring module, which is the key's leading segment. Joined with "key" by a dot to form the full key, which must be declared with read-write tenant access.
parameters.name: namespace

parameters.description: The rest of the setting key under the namespace; dots are allowed. Joined with the namespace by a dot to form the full key, which must be declared with read-write tenant access.
parameters.name: key

400.description: A layer or tenant query parameter was sent, or the tenant in the path is outside its value domain

403.description: The caller holds no settings.tenant.write in the tenant's domain, the caller has not proved an email address (contact-required), the item is declared read-only (read-only), or the host's settings write seam refused the write (protected)

404.description: The full key is not declared or exposes no tenant access

delete.summary: Drop the tenant layer's explicit row for one setting

put.description: Writes one row for the setting named by the namespace and key path segments on the layer of the tenant in the path. The full key `<namespace>.<key>` must match a declared item the tenant surface exposes. A key with no tenant access, whether undeclared or declared on the platform surface alone, is 404 — the same answer an undeclared key gets. An item declared read-only is 403 read-only: it is visible, and the refusal names why the write cannot be made rather than hiding the item. A value of the mask string a sensitive item is shown as is 422 masked-value before the seam, the audit and the store. A write turning a boolean switch off while the platform layer holds it on is 409 tenant-admission-enforced, also before the seam, the audit and the store. The host's settings write seam is asked before anything is changed; a refusal is 403 protected and an unreadable answer is 503. The value is encoded under the item's declared type and then held to its declared domain; a value that cannot be encoded, lies outside the domain, or exceeds the size limit answers 422. A mandatory audit row is written before the change, and if it cannot be written the setting is left untouched and the answer is 503. The change is attributed to the caller's accountability key, which under an impersonation is the administrator making the request rather than the account impersonated. Success is 204 with no body.

parameters.description: The tenant's name in the path. The path-tenant layer resolves it to the internal identifier before the handler runs; the write lands on that tenant's settings layer, and a "layer" or "tenant" query parameter is refused with 400.
parameters.name: tenant

parameters.description: The namespace of the item to write: the declaring module, which is the key's leading segment. Joined with "key" by a dot to form the full key, which must be declared with read-write tenant access.
parameters.name: namespace

parameters.description: The rest of the setting key under the namespace; dots are allowed. Joined with the namespace by a dot to form the full key, which must be declared with read-write tenant access.
parameters.name: key

value.description: The value to store, in the JSON form the item's declared type is read from: a boolean for a switch. It is encoded under the declared type and then held to the item's declared domain; a value that cannot be encoded, lies outside the domain, or exceeds the size limit answers 422. The mask string a sensitive item is shown as is refused with 422 masked-value before anything runs.

requestBody.description: The write's body: exactly one object, whose `value` member carries the value to store.

400.description: A layer or tenant query parameter was sent, the tenant in the path is outside its value domain, or the body is not one object

403.description: The caller holds no settings.tenant.write in the tenant's domain, the caller has not proved an email address (contact-required), the item is declared read-only (read-only), or the host's settings write seam refused the write (protected)

404.description: The full key is not declared or exposes no tenant access

409.description: The write would turn off a policy the platform layer requires (tenant-admission-enforced)

413.description: The request body is over the endpoint's limit

415.description: The request body is not application/json

422.description: The value is the mask string a sensitive item is shown as (masked-value), cannot be encoded under the declared type, or lies outside its declared domain

put.summary: Write one setting row on the tenant layer
